citation.title: Roles of KSTAR toward reactor-relevant diagnostics

topic: Status review of KSTAR diagnostics mapped to reactor requirements; integrated, inference-based and virtual diagnostic frameworks
own_question: How can KSTAR diagnostics, synthetic diagnostics and Bayesian or ML inference support reduced, robust reactor diagnostic sets?
actual_method_and_evidence: Narrative review. It contains no new experiments or analysis. It summarizes cited KSTAR work, including NN-CES real-time analysis of CES spectra trained on roughly 150k frames [Lee 2021 RSI], Kalman magnetic–Hall sensor fusion, and real-time density control. It also proposes channel-ablation, information-gain and observability criteria, but does not demonstrate them.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: The review notes that CES provides routine Ti and rotation profiles on KSTAR. It cites a neural-network approach (NN-CES) for real-time analysis of CES spectra. This supports framing NN-CES as upstream spectral reading.
claim_checks.original_pdf_locator: p.8-9 (Sec.3 text after sixth example); Table 2(a) CES row
claim_checks.qualification: The review only reports these claims and cites the primary paper. Cite Lee et al 2021 RSI for NN-CES specifics. The review does not say whether the measured species is impurity or main-ion, and gives no latency figures.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: The review frames sparse-measurement state estimation as a reactor-relevant motivation. It treats Bayesian or ML reconstruction from reduced sensor sets, and evaluation by removing channels, as a stated research direction.
claim_checks.original_pdf_locator: Sec.5, p.14 paragraph on mandatory vs auxiliary diagnostics; Table 1 last row
claim_checks.qualification: This is the authors' perspective; no quantitative demonstration is reported. The review also notes that CES depends on a neutral beam and optical access, which limits its use in a reactor.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Gives no CES report cadence, arrival latency, or BES/ECEI nowcasting.
forbidden_inferences: Do not treat the review as evidence that NN-CES achieves a particular latency or accuracy.
Do not claim the review validates nowcasting or the use of BES/ECEI to inform CES.
Do not cite reactor requirement targets as performance KSTAR has achieved.
Do not infer that prior KSTAR inference work is noncausal or electron-only.
Do not claim the review's ablation and information-gain workflow has been implemented.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Optional context for motivating integrated inference from sparse diagnostics and for placing NN-CES upstream. The primary NN-CES paper should carry the specific claims.
